plan: [In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding my true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Since this is a one-round game and values are independent, bidding $46 maximizes expected payoff: I win when my value exceeds others' bids and pay the second-highest. Other rational bidders will anticipate truth-telling; their beliefs do not change that bidding my value is optimal. Bids are allowed in $0.1 increments, so I'll submit 46.]

[In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true private value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected payoff regardless of others' bids. Overbidding risks negative surplus if you pay above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Given my value is $17 and opponents are rational, I will bid 17.]

[In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. With my private value $28, I will bid $28. This avoids overpaying while ensuring I win whenever the highest opponent value (and thus their bid) is below 28. Bids are in $0.1 increments, so $28 is valid. Tie-breaking is random, but truthful bidding still maximizes expected payoff.]
